lead: A refusal `nvs-db` builds with `io::Error::other` reaches a program as `Core\Db\DbError`, whatever its wording says.
body: That crate builds no fault of its own, so the `io::ErrorKind` is the only thing carrying a class across the boundary: `statement_failure` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/db/bind.rs:186`) reads `InvalidInput` as a mistake in the call and everything else as the engine's own refusal. Build a refusal about the *call* — a busy connection, a value with no bound form — with `io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput`, and prove it with a `.nvst` case catching the class the rule names.
